question: Suman and Sujata travel the same distance at speeds of 10 km/hr and 12 km/hr respectively. If Suman takes 36 minutes more than Sujata, the distance traveled by each is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, Distance = (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ − S₂) × Δt

⇒ Time difference Δt = 36 minutes = 36 ÷ 60 hours = 3 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ Distance = (10 × 12) ÷ (12 − 10) × (3 ÷ 5)

⇒ Distance = (120 ÷ 2) × (3 ÷ 5) = 60 × 0.6

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Suman = 10 km/hr

Speed of Sujata = 12 km/hr

Difference in time = 36 minutes = 36 ÷ 60 = 3 ÷ 5 hours

 Suman: 10 km/hr (T + 36 min)
 
 

 Sujata: 12 km/hr (T min)

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the distance traveled by each be 'D' km.

⇒ Time taken by Suman − Time taken by Sujata = 3 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ (D ÷ 10) − (D ÷ 12) = 3 ÷ 5

⇒ (6D − 5D) ÷ 60 = 3 ÷ 5

⇒ D ÷ 60 = 3 ÷ 5

⇒ D = (3 × 60) ÷ 5

⇒ D = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional. A ratio of speeds = a : b means the ratio of time taken will be = b : a.

Average Speed (Same Distance)

If equal distances are covered at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, then the Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
